# Execution limits and public supervision

The submitted Python entry and its Rust build/engine children share one request wall envelope: wall 180 s; per-process
CPU soft 180/hard 181 s; address space 2 GiB; 64 processes/threads per isolated
UID (including trusted wrapper processes during the public check); 256 FDs; 64 MiB per file written; core size 0. Stdout <=32 MiB; stderr <=1 MiB.
Exit zero and emit exactly one valid schema-conforming JSON document. Empty,
non-JSON, duplicate-key/nonfinite JSON, extra output, nonzero exit, and exceeded
limits fail. Normal text, `.buffer`, raw descriptors 0/1, `fileno`, `fdopen`,
and explicitly written/flushed JSON followed by `os._exit(0)` are supported.
No CPU affinity is imposed by the task-local runner. Formal CPU allocation
is 2 CPUs; shared-host local timings have no throughput-ranking interpretation.

The local worker uses a nonprivileged UID in a chroot with no-new-privileges.
It denies sockets/connect, SysV shared memory/semaphores/messages, kill/tkill/tgkill
signals, ptrace and process_vm access, namespace/mount/chroot/session/group changes,
credential changes, file handles, BPF/keys/perf/userfaultfd/io_uring/pidfd_getfd.
Clone namespace/privilege flags are denied; clone3 returns ENOSYS. Ordinary
subprocesses/threads remain subject to the process limit. The x86_64 syscall
ABI is required. No additional h-profile fork/thread prohibition applies.
The exact denied syscall names are: socket, socketpair, connect, shmget,
shmat, shmctl, semget, semop, semctl, semtimedop, msgget, msgsnd, msgrcv,
msgctl, kill, tkill, tgkill, ptrace, process_vm_readv, process_vm_writev,
unshare, setns, mount, umount2, pivot_root, chroot, setsid, setpgid, setuid,
setgid, setreuid, setregid, setresuid, setresgid, setgroups, open_by_handle_at,
name_to_handle_at, bpf, keyctl, add_key, request_key, perf_event_open,
userfaultfd, io_uring_setup, io_uring_enter, io_uring_register, pidfd_getfd.
These return EPERM. clone flags intersecting 0x7e820000 return EPERM;
clone3 returns ENOSYS. Non-x86_64 and x32 syscall ABIs kill the process.
Scratch has a sampled emergency brake at 1 GiB accounted bytes or 50000
entries (checked about every 250 ms); crossing it is infrastructure failure,
not a task score. This is not a hard aggregate quota. Local chroot shares the
host kernel; formal cgroup/storage/transport attestation remains pending.

Run `python3 public_check.py [--candidate submission/main.py]`. It refuses
root execution and launches a bounded child via actual stdin/stdout pipes;
only public fixtures are used. Run inside the supplied nonroot environment.
It restores the full scored syscall policy and the stated per-process limits
in each candidate before executing its bytes. Ordinary child processes and
threads remain permitted, within the same existing 64-process/thread UID limit.
The trusted checker owns a new session/process group per invocation and is a
child subreaper. It terminates the whole group and reaps adopted descendants
before accepting output or reporting failure, including when the candidate
returns normally with detached descendant streams. Cleanup also runs on the
180-second deadline, either output cap, abnormal/nonzero exit, and SIGTERM or
SIGINT. Repeated interruption records cancellation without interrupting cleanup.
Each invocation has a separate 5-second cleanup allowance; cleanup failure is
an infrastructure error with no public PASS. Finite JSON includes exponent
forms: overflowing numbers such as `1e999` are rejected gracefully.

The trusted checker parent requires a development supervision profile, distinct
from scored candidate execution. Relative to the scored default worker, that
parent alone may call kill, tkill, tgkill, setsid and setpgid for ordinary
same-UID supervision. Its per-process CPU limit is soft 1800/hard 1801 seconds;
all other worker deny rules, memory/FD/file/core/process limits, UID/chroot,
scratch checks and inherited CPU affinity are unchanged. Its full-command
outer wall envelope is 1720 seconds, with 1 MiB stdout and 1 MiB stderr. These
wrapper allowances cover all nine sequential public checks and their cleanup;
every candidate invocation still has the exact scored 180-second wall and
180/181-second CPU limits, original deny policy, and 32 MiB/1 MiB output caps.
The public `candidate_policy.py` installs that full policy after the trusted
launcher creates the group, so candidates cannot change session/group or send
kill/tkill/tgkill signals. A scored-profile parent without supervision permission
fails before executing a candidate. On an authoring host, the A-owned local
public-check entry selects the checker profile; scored runs retain the original
worker binary. This is a wrapper implementation detail, not a submission change.
The image's offline container boundary supplies filesystem/network isolation;
the public checker itself is not a security boundary. On the authoring host,
use the documented task-private sandbox entry rather than executing a candidate
directly as host root. Public fixtures are examples, not hidden truth.

The image build installs only the bundled checksum-pinned compiler archives;
no dependency download is needed. The compiler entry rustc configures its
library path; build.sh/build.py use the same /opt/rust installation.
